- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often underestimates upside; add 3–8% buffer to forecast mean for first 10 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) and model is still rising, force downward correction by 5–10% to align with sentiment drift.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if recent 3–5 days show mean reversion or volatility decay, reduce forecast slope by 15–25% to avoid overfitting to recent spikes.
- When official events are high-frequency (e.g., 20+ events/30d), model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter to forecast, especially if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
